characteristics.cultivar: Camellia sinensis var. assamica (Yunnan large-leaf cultivar)

description.short: Golden black tea from Yunnan buds, sweet and malty with a honeyed aroma
description.overview: Crafted from the same large-leaf var. assamica material used for Yunnan pu-erh, but processed with full black tea oxidation, yielding an exceptionally rich and malty profile.
description.leaf: Slender golden buds covered in down (in premium grades) or larger dark leaves with golden tips (in standard grades)
description.liquor: Bright golden-red, rich and clear liquor
description.aroma: Honey, malt, sweet potato, dried fruits
description.taste: Sweet, malty, full-bodied, without harsh astringency
description.processing: Plucking → withering → rolling → full oxidation → drying

history.origin: Developed in the late 1930s when Chinese tea experts sought to enter the international black tea market and compete with Indian and Ceylon teas
history.development: Yunnan's large-leaf var. assamica proved exceptionally well suited for producing full-bodied, malty black tea with strength comparable to Assam teas
history.modern: Premium grades consisting entirely of golden downy buds (such as Golden Needle or Yunnan Gold) are today prized among China's most celebrated black teas
interestingFacts: Dian Hong became one of China's major export teas in the 20th century, specifically formulated to appeal to Western palates accustomed to bold black teas
It uses the exact same botanical variety (var. assamica) as famous Yunnan pu-erh, yet yields a completely different flavor profile through black tea processing
